title: Bounded memory representation
statement: Let $W$ be a natural-number word width, let $L$ consist of an integer word bound and natural-number space and depth bounds, let $\mu$ assign an integer to each natural-numbered address, and let $m$ assign a $W$-bit word to each integer address. The representation is valid if, for every natural-numbered address $a$, $m(a)$ is the $W$-bit encoding of $\mu(a)$, and $|\mu(a)|$ is at most the integer word bound in $L$.
hypotheses_covered: The word width $W$ is a natural number
The limits $L$ contain an integer word bound and natural-number space and depth bounds
At each natural-numbered address, the stored word is the encoding of its assigned integer
Each assigned integer has absolute value at most the word bound
